title: Awami League leaders visit Petrapole border as Hasina's planned December return nears
dek: Four senior leaders of the banned party, living in Kolkata, spent about two hours at the busiest India-Bangladesh land crossing on Sunday, according to reports. Indian and Bangladeshi officials have not commented.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Four senior leaders of Bangladesh's Awami League who have been living in India visited the Petrapole land port in North 24 Parganas on Sunday, in what reports in both countries described as a survey of possible routes for the return of former prime minister Sheikh Hasina, who has said she will go back to Bangladesh in December.

The group, which reports identified as presidium members Jahangir Kabir Nanak and Mofazzal Hossain Chowdhury Maya, joint general secretary AFM Bahauddin Nasim and former MP Alauddin Ahmed Chowdhury Nasim, arrived at Petrapole at about 2 pm and left at about 3.50 pm after a closed-door meeting in the immigration area, according to reports. Reporters at the scene said the group used an entrance separate from the one used by the public. Officials of the immigration department, the Border Security Force and Petrapole police declined to comment, according to reports.

## What we know and do not know

Neither the Awami League, the Ministry of External Affairs nor Bangladesh's foreign ministry had made any statement on the visit by Monday afternoon. Reports citing Indian television channels said the leaders planned to visit the Tripura border and the route between Agartala's airport and Bangladesh's Akhaura crossing next, on Tuesday and Wednesday; those plans have not been confirmed.

Two of the four face cases at Bangladesh's International Crimes Tribunal, which is trying people accused over the crackdown on the July 2024 uprising. Mr Nanak is on trial, and Mr Bahauddin Nasim has been sentenced to death in his absence in a separate case, according to reports. The interim government banned the Awami League's activities in 2025.

On the same day, Hindu and Matua groups held a rally at Petrapole demanding the release of the jailed Hindu monk Chinmoy Krishna Das. The state's Food Minister Ashok Kirtania and Bangaon Dakshin BJP MLA Swapan Majumdar attended. "Wait and watch. Hasina could enter Bangladesh through the Petrapole border," Mr Majumdar said, according to reports.

## Dhaka's position

Bangladesh's government has said Ms Hasina can return only through extradition to face the courts. Ms Hasina, who fled to India in August 2024 and was sentenced to death in her absence in November 2025, has applied for a passport through the Bangladesh High Commission; the first application was rejected and her lawyers filed a second request on 19 November, according to reports. State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humayun Kabir has said Bangladesh "does not give passports to terrorists", according to reports, and Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has accused India of "conspiring" against Bangladesh.

India's MEA has said that anyone travelling would need a travel document, and spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said on 20 November that India wanted "a positive, constructive and forward-looking relationship with Bangladesh".

## Why it matters for Bengal

Petrapole, opposite Benapole in Bangladesh, is the busiest land port in South Asia and handles a large share of India-Bangladesh trade and passenger traffic through Bengal. Any attempt by Ms Hasina to cross there would put the Bongaon area at the centre of a diplomatic and security confrontation. Bangladesh has deployed 90 more platoons of its Border Guard Bangladesh after a wave of arson attacks in which ruling-party supporters accuse Awami League activists, and has tightened patrols along the border, according to reports.

## What happens next

Ms Hasina has not announced a date or route for her return; some Awami League leaders in Bengal have spoken of mid-December, according to reports. The MEA's next weekly briefing, usually on Thursday or Friday, is the likeliest place for an official Indian comment.
